messages:
matt: Heads up — hit a packaging/lock mismatch between my mac dev env and CI today.
laura: ugh what happened?
matt: On mac (arm64) poetry.lock pulled a source package for a conditional dep, CI (linux amd64) tried to install a manylinux wheel and pip failed with an incompatible wheel error.
samir: paste the error?
matt: sure:
ERROR: Package 'somelib' requires a different Python: 3.11.0 not in '>=3.10, <3.11'
Collecting somelib-1.2.3-cp311-cp311-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl
  ERROR: somelib-1.2.3-cp311-cp311-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl is not a supported wheel on this platform.
ivy: sounds like poetry.lock was generated on mac and included different resolved artifacts due to environment markers. Did you run `poetry lock` on mac?
matt: yup. I assumed lockfiles are platform-agnostic but markers in pyproject (os_name/platform_machine) are causing different resolution. Example: 
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
requests = "^2.31"
httpx = { version = "^0.25", optional = true }
async = { version = "^0.1", markers = "python_version >= \"3.10\" and sys_platform != \"win32\"" }
laura: those markers mean the resolver chooses different distributions per platform.
samir: common trap: devs on mac generate lock excluding linux-only sdists/wheels. CI then hits unexpected wheels.
matt: CI runs `poetry install --no-root` on linux runners. The exported requirements referenced a mac-only source and pip attempted a linux wheel incompatible with our python.
ivy: workarounds: 1) generate lock inside a linux container to match CI 2) use `poetry export --format requirements.txt --platform manylinux2014_x86_64` to resolve for target platform.
laura: note `--platform` requires a recent poetry and resolver support. Use `--extras` to include optional deps like async.
samir: alternate: remove strict platform markers and do runtime guards, or pin problematic deps to sdist/wheel you control.
matt: Also saw missing async extras: locally I had `httpx[http2]` via extras but CI lock didn't include it. Runtime error: 
AttributeError: 'Client' object has no attribute 'stream_async'
ivy: add extras group for the async client and a CI smoke test that imports the async module.
laura: propose action items:
- standardize lock generation inside linux container in our dev guide
- add `poetry export --platform` step in CI to ensure platform-specific wheel choices are reproducible
- add an integration that imports `redwood.async_client` to validate extras
matt: quick command for local dev: `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src -w /src python:3.11-slim bash -c "pip install poetry && poetry lock --no-update"`
samir: immediate unblock: I forced CI to `pip install --no-binary somelib` so it built from sdist — slower but worked.
ivy: I'll open a small PR to onboarding docs recommending lock generation in linux and add the CI export step.
laura: could devex-bot help? maybe add a lint rule to remind to regen `poetry.lock` when `pyproject.toml` changes.
devex-bot: Noted — creating issue #DEVEX-412: "enforce poetry.lock regen when pyproject changes"
matt: one more gotcha: editable installs can hide missing extras locally. Recommend non-editable installs in CI so missing deps fail fast.
ivy: I'll add checklist to PR: regenerate lock in linux, export with platform, non-editable CI install, add async import smoke test.
matt: thanks all, saved my afternoon :) :thumbsup:
laura: :party_parrot:
